sentences.en: Today's episode is brought to you by T-Mobile for Business.
sentences.zh: 本期节目由 T-Mobile for Business 赞助播出。

sentences.en: Many years ago, when I was a child, my mother told me a family story.
sentences.zh: 很多年前，我还是个孩子的时候，母亲给我讲过一个家族故事。

sentences.en: It had to do with her brother, my uncle.
sentences.zh: 那是关于她哥哥，也就是我舅舅的故事。

sentences.en: He was an extremely creative man with varied interests in books and music and art.
sentences.zh: 他是一个极具创造力的人，对书籍、音乐和艺术都有着广泛的兴趣。

sentences.en: He could also be a little, how shall I put this, disorganized.
sentences.zh: 但怎么说呢，他有时也有点……不拘小节。

sentences.en: My uncle was the kind of person who was always ready to reminisce, and he was an amazing storyteller.
sentences.zh: 我舅舅是个随时准备追忆往事的人，而且他是一位了不起的讲故事高手。

sentences.en: He could spin the tiniest events into funny stories that had you laughing until you cried.
sentences.zh: 他能把最琐碎的小事讲成妙趣横生的故事，让你笑得前仰后合。

sentences.en: Anyway, the story my mother told me had to do with my uncle's wedding day.
sentences.zh: 总之，母亲讲的那个故事是关于舅舅婚礼当天的。

sentences.en: On his way to the wedding venue, my uncle suddenly remembered he had forgotten to invite a dear friend and fellow storyteller.
sentences.zh: 在去婚礼现场的路上，舅舅突然想起忘了邀请一位挚友，那也是位讲故事的行家。

sentences.en: So he took a detour and went to the barber shop to make sure his friend came to the wedding.
sentences.zh: 于是他绕道去了理发店，一定要确保他的朋友能来参加婚礼。

sentences.en: When he got to the shop, the barber was busy with his customers and asked my uncle to wait while he finished.
sentences.zh: 当他赶到店里时，理发师正忙着招待客人，便让舅舅等他忙完。

sentences.en: My uncle happily settled down, and he and the barber traded funny stories as the scissors went snip-snip.
sentences.zh: 舅舅愉快地坐了下来，伴随着剪刀“咔嚓咔嚓”的声音，他和理发师互相讲起了趣事。

sentences.en: All this time, of course, the guests at the wedding and the prospective bride were getting increasingly alarmed.
sentences.zh: 当然，与此同时，婚礼上的宾客和准新娘却越来越焦急。

sentences.en: Had something happened to the groom?
When my uncle finally showed up, his barber triumphantly in tow, he had no idea why everyone was upset.
sentences.zh: 当舅舅终于带着理发师凯旋而归时，他完全不明白大家为什么那么生气。

sentences.en: I've always loved that story because it perfectly captured my uncle's attitude toward life.
sentences.zh: 我一直很喜欢这个故事，因为它完美地捕捉到了舅舅的人生态度。
截止日期和预约都可以往后排。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, we explore the world of family stories, how these stories shape who we become,
sentences.zh: 本周在《隐藏的大脑》中，我们将探索家族故事的世界，了解这些故事如何塑造我们的成长，

sentences.en: and the fascinating science that demonstrates why telling certain kinds of stories can make us happier, healthier, and better people.
sentences.zh: 以及迷人的科学研究如何证明，讲述特定类型的故事能让我们变得更快乐、更健康、更好。

sentences.en: Cultures around the world have occasions that are designed for people to gather, chat, and reminisce.
sentences.zh: 世界各地的文化中都有一些旨在让人们聚在一起、聊天和追忆往事的场合。

sentences.en: This can happen on birthdays, on anniversaries, and at funerals.
sentences.zh: 这可能发生在生日、纪念日或葬礼上。

sentences.en: Family members remind each other about the ties that bind them together.
sentences.zh: 家庭成员会互相提醒那些将他们紧密联系在一起的纽带。

sentences.en: Disputes break out over half-remembered events from decades ago.
sentences.zh: 关于几十年前那些记忆模糊的往事，争论也会随之爆发。

sentences.en: At Emory University, psychologist Robin Feivusch studies the psychological effects these stories can have on our lives.
sentences.zh: 在埃默里大学，心理学家罗宾·菲武什正在研究这些故事对我们生活产生的心理影响。

sentences.en: Robin Feivusch, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 罗宾·菲武什，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm so privileged to be here.
sentences.zh: 能来到这里我深感荣幸。

sentences.en: I really am looking forward to this interview.
sentences.zh: 我真的很期待这次采访。

sentences.en: Robin, when you were very young, your family was struck by two terrible tragedies, more or less simultaneously.
sentences.zh: 罗宾，当你还很小的时候，你的家庭几乎同时遭遇了两场可怕的悲剧。

sentences.en: It changed the course of your life.
sentences.zh: 这改变了你的人生轨迹。

sentences.en: Can you tell me what happened?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我发生了什么吗？

sentences.en: Well, my father died when I was quite young, and my mother was in a very, very bad car accident.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我父亲在我很小的时候就去世了，而我母亲当时出了一场非常非常严重的车祸。

sentences.en: She went through the passenger side window of the windshield, was thrown out of the car, and she was actually in a coma for six weeks.
sentences.zh: 她从副驾驶座的挡风玻璃飞了出去，被甩出了车外，实际上昏迷了六个星期。

sentences.en: So she was in a coma when my father died.
sentences.zh: 所以父亲去世时，她还在昏迷中。

sentences.en: And she had a lot of bodily fractures, as you might imagine.
sentences.zh: 而且你可以想象，她身上有多处骨折。

sentences.en: She was in a body caSt.
sentences.zh: 她当时全身都打着石膏。

sentences.en: But she also had a lot of cognitive damage and was essentially in and out of hospitals for a number of years.
sentences.zh: 但她也有严重的认知损伤，基本上有几年时间都在医院进进出出。

sentences.en: So my grandparents raised me and my sister for most of my childhood.
sentences.zh: 所以我的童年大部分时间是由祖父母抚养我和姐姐长大的。

sentences.en: And during that time, we spent, frankly, quite a lot of time in hospital waiting rooms and not spending time doing many of the typical activities of childhood.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，那段时间我们花了很多时间在医院候诊室里，没能像普通孩子那样参加很多典型的童年活动。

sentences.en: If I could ask you, what happened to your dad?
sentences.zh: 能问一下，你父亲是怎么去世的吗？

sentences.en: How did he come to pass away at an early age?
And how old were you at the time, Robin?
Oh, so you were very young.
You probably have very few memories of your dad.
sentences.zh: 你对父亲的记忆可能非常少。

sentences.en: It's one of the things that actually got me interested in studying memory is I was very young.
sentences.zh: 这正是让我对研究记忆产生兴趣的原因之一，因为我当时太小了。

sentences.en: And most people can't remember things that happened before they were about three or three and a half.
sentences.zh: 大多数人无法记住三岁或三岁半之前发生的事情。

sentences.en: That's a very strong research finding.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常确凿的研究发现。

sentences.en: When you ask adults to recall their earliest childhood memories, they almost never remember anything that happened before they were three.
sentences.zh: 当你让成年人回忆他们最早的童年记忆时，他们几乎记不起三岁之前发生的任何事情。

sentences.en: But I have this unfortunate marker in my childhood.
sentences.zh: 但我童年里有这样一个不幸的标记。

sentences.en: I know if I remember my father, it had to be something that happened before I was three.
sentences.zh: 我知道如果我对父亲有记忆，那一定发生在我三岁之前。

sentences.en: And I actually have two memories of my father.
sentences.zh: 我确实对父亲有两个记忆。

sentences.en: They're very strong images and sense perceptions of being with him.
sentences.zh: 那是关于和他在一起时非常强烈的画面和感官知觉。

sentences.en: Can you tell me what those two memories are?
sentences.zh: 能告诉我那两个记忆是什么吗？

sentences.en: One is actually we were visiting caverns, underground caverns in upstate New York.
sentences.zh: 其中一个是我们在参观纽约州北部的洞穴，地下洞穴。

sentences.en: I believe they're called house caverns.
sentences.zh: 我想它们被称为豪斯洞穴。

sentences.en: My sister is about three years older than me.
sentences.zh: 我姐姐比我大三岁左右。

sentences.en: My mother, my father, and I was on my father's shoulders.
sentences.zh: 我母亲、父亲和我，当时我骑在父亲的肩膀上。

sentences.en: And I remember the feeling of being on his shoulders.
sentences.zh: 我记得骑在他肩膀上的那种感觉。

sentences.en: And then suddenly things going very dark because they turned off all the lights in the cave and feeling safe.
sentences.zh: 然后突然间，因为他们关掉了洞穴里所有的灯，周围变得一片漆黑，但我感到很安全。

sentences.en: And you felt safe, of course, because you were sitting on your father's shoulders.
sentences.zh: 当然，你感到安全是因为你坐在父亲的肩膀上。

sentences.en: I was sitting on his shoulders.
And, of course, obviously, that's a super meaningful memory to me because I have so little of my father,
sentences.zh: 当然，显而易见，这对我来说是一个非常有意义的记忆，因为我对父亲的记忆太少了，

sentences.en: so little of that security of having my father there to protect me and support me.
sentences.zh: 那种有父亲在身边保护我、支持我的安全感太少了。

sentences.en: The other memory is much more mundane.
sentences.zh: 另一个记忆就平凡多了。

sentences.en: I remember him giving me a bath.
The twin tragedies of her father's death and her mother's injuries devastated the family.
sentences.zh: 父亲去世和母亲受伤的双重悲剧摧毁了这个家庭。

sentences.en: Of course, Robin was too young to fully understand what was happening.
sentences.zh: 当然，罗宾当时太小了，无法完全理解发生了什么。
我敢肯定那一定非常令人心碎。

sentences.en: So my experience was just my life was yanked out, but I didn't have a full cognitive understanding of the context and what was going on.
sentences.zh: 所以我的经历只是生活突然被连根拔起，但我对背景和正在发生的事情没有完整的认知理解。

sentences.en: And so my memories from that period are very fragmentary and really not very coherent in the way.
sentences.zh: 所以那段时期的记忆非常零碎，而且在某种程度上并不连贯。

sentences.en: And frankly, my family, their way of dealing with it was just never to talk about it.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，我的家人处理这件事的方式就是绝口不提。

sentences.en: I mean, I can imagine at one level this must have been so painful and even recollecting these events must have been so painful.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我可以想象在某种层面上这一定非常痛苦，即使是回忆这些事件也一定非常痛苦。

sentences.en: And perhaps they were worried that you were very small and talking to you about something that was painful might have hurt you.
sentences.zh: 也许他们担心你还很小，和你谈论痛苦的事情可能会伤害到你。

sentences.en: So I can imagine that those might have been the impulses that caused people to say, let's not talk about it.
sentences.zh: 所以我可以想象，这可能是导致人们说“我们别谈这个了”的动机。

sentences.en: I think that is part of it.
sentences.zh: 我想这确实是原因之一。

sentences.en: And I want to come back to that.
sentences.zh: 我想回头再谈谈这一点。

sentences.en: I think for my family, that was definitely part of it.
sentences.zh: 我想对于我的家庭来说，这绝对是原因的一部分。

sentences.en: The other part of it was just, frankly, my grandmother's personality.
sentences.zh: 另一部分原因坦白说就是我祖母的性格。

sentences.en: So she went through a lot of hard times and her way of dealing with it, with all of it was, let's, we just don't revisit that.
sentences.zh: 她经历了很多艰难时刻，她处理所有事情的方式就是：我们不去重提那些事。

sentences.en: We just don't go back there.
sentences.zh: 我们不去触碰那些过去。

sentences.en: Quite frankly, when I would ask her questions about her past, my past, my family's past, the answer was always, why do you need to know that?
sentences.zh: 坦白说，当我问她关于她的过去、我的过去、我们家庭的过去时，答案总是：你为什么要问这些？

sentences.en: In time, Robin would come to study the role that family stories play in the psychological well-being of both children and their caregivers.
sentences.zh: 后来，罗宾开始研究家族故事在儿童及其照料者的心理健康中所扮演的角色。
但那是很久以后的事了。

sentences.en: As a child, Robin wasn't comparing what happened in her family to what happened in other families.
sentences.zh: 小时候，罗宾并没有将自己家庭发生的事情与别人家进行比较。
我并没有真正注意到这一点。

sentences.en: And until, I didn't notice it until I met my first husband's family.
sentences.zh: 直到我遇到了第一任丈夫的家人，我才注意到。

sentences.en: And I started to spend a lot of time with them.
sentences.zh: 我开始花很多时间和他们在一起。

sentences.en: And they were a huge family, a family storytelling family.
sentences.zh: 他们是一个大家庭，一个喜欢讲故事的家庭。

sentences.en: They told stories, like many, many families, all the time.
sentences.zh: 像许多许多家庭一样，他们一直在讲故事。

sentences.en: But they had all the kinds of family stories.
sentences.zh: 但他们有各种各样的家族故事。

sentences.en: They had the everyday, tell me about your day-to-day, what happened, sharing their own, remember, this is like when we went to the beach last summer.
sentences.zh: 他们有日常琐事，比如“告诉我你今天过得怎么样，发生了什么”，分享他们自己的经历，比如“记得吗，就像去年夏天我们去海滩的时候”。

sentences.en: And they had the big, iconic stories every Thanksgiving, every Thanksgiving, the story about how one of the uncles crashed the car through the trees when he was a teenager,
sentences.zh: 他们还有那些标志性的经典故事，每年感恩节，一定要讲那个关于其中一位舅舅在青少年时期开车撞进树林里的故事，

sentences.en: And it had to get told the same way, with the same punchlines, every year.
sentences.zh: 而且每年都必须以同样的方式、同样的笑点讲出来。

sentences.en: And I started to realize how important that was to keep that family cemented as a happy, healthy family.
sentences.zh: 我开始意识到，这对于维系家庭作为一个幸福、健康的整体是多么重要。

sentences.en: Yeah, so it's not the information in that uncle car crash story that was important, because everybody knew the facts already.
sentences.zh: 是的，所以那个舅舅撞车故事里的信息并不重要，因为每个人都已经知道事实了。

sentences.en: Everybody knew every detail of the story.
sentences.zh: 每个人都知道故事的每一个细节。

sentences.en: If you told it the wrong way, everybody would correct you.
sentences.zh: 如果你讲错了，每个人都会纠正你。

sentences.en: And what went through your heart when you saw that?
sentences.zh: 当你看到这些时，你心里是什么感受？

sentences.en: I mean, you must have been happy to be part of this family that had this rich family lore.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你一定很高兴能成为这个拥有丰富家族传说的家庭的一员。

sentences.en: But was there a part of you that sort of said, that noticed that you didn't have that?
sentences.zh: 但有没有一部分的你，注意到自己并没有这些经历？

sentences.en: I mean, is that how you, was that made aware to you?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你是这样意识到这一点的吗？

sentences.en: I mean, it was such a contrast that it was so different than the way my family interacted.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这种对比太强烈了，和我们家人的互动方式完全不同。

sentences.en: As Robin became a researcher, she was to learn that family stories are not just family stories.
sentences.zh: 当罗宾成为研究员后，她了解到家族故事不仅仅是家族故事。

sentences.en: They are much more than dinner table conversation or fodder for Thanksgiving table punchlines.
sentences.zh: 它们远不止是餐桌上的谈资，也不是感恩节饭桌上的笑料。

sentences.en: Family stories turn out to play a crucial role in the mental health of the people who tell the stories
sentences.zh: 事实证明，家族故事在讲述者的心理健康中起着至关重要的作用，

sentences.en: and the mental health of the people who listen to the stories.
sentences.zh: 同时也影响着倾听者的心理健康。

sentences.en: They can serve as anchors for identity and self-esteem.
sentences.zh: 它们可以作为身份认同和自尊的锚点。

sentences.en: Told right, they can change the direction of our lives.
sentences.zh: 如果讲述得当，它们甚至能改变我们人生的方向。
你正在收听的是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Robin Fiversh is a psychologist at Emory University who studies the way parents and children communicate.
sentences.zh: 罗宾·菲武什是埃默里大学的一位心理学家，专门研究父母与子女的沟通方式。

sentences.en: Early on in her career, she spent extended amounts of time with families,
sentences.zh: 在她职业生涯的早期，她花了大量时间与家庭相处，

sentences.en: listening to how parents talked with children.
sentences.zh: 倾听父母如何与孩子交谈。

sentences.en: I was interested in how families, particularly mothers, talked with their 3-, 4-, 5-year-old children
sentences.zh: 我对家庭，特别是母亲，如何与她们三、四、五岁的孩子谈论，

sentences.en: about the events of the child's life.
sentences.zh: 孩子生活中的事件很感兴趣。

sentences.en: So we did a lot of work where we would visit families in their homes and hang out with them,
sentences.zh: 所以我们做了很多工作，去家里拜访这些家庭，和他们待在一起，

sentences.en: and then we would explicitly ask mothers to sit down with their child
sentences.zh: 然后我们会明确要求母亲坐下来和孩子一起，

sentences.en: and talk about some things that have happened, some special occurrences.
sentences.zh: 谈论一些发生过的事情，一些特别的经历。

sentences.en: We gave them very few instructions, and we looked at how the past got reconstructed.
sentences.zh: 我们给他们的指导很少，我们观察过去是如何被重构的。

sentences.en: And we discovered that this was really an important part of children learning how to narrate their own past,
sentences.zh: 我们发现，这对于孩子学习如何叙述自己的过去确实是一个重要的部分，

sentences.en: and also that it actually helped children increase their ability to remember the paSt.
sentences.zh: 而且它实际上还帮助孩子提高了记忆过去的能力。

sentences.en: We found that different mothers do this in different ways,
sentences.zh: 我们发现不同的母亲以不同的方式做这件事，

sentences.en: and it has a lot of consequences, not only for how children remember things,
sentences.zh: 这不仅对孩子如何记忆事物有很大影响，

sentences.en: but how they feel about themselves.
sentences.zh: 而且对他们如何看待自己也有很大影响。

sentences.en: So mothers and children who are more elaborate and detailed in these kinds of early memory conversations
sentences.zh: 所以，那些在这些早期记忆对话中更具阐述性和细节性的母亲和孩子

sentences.en: have children who have higher self-esteem even very early in development.
sentences.zh: 拥有在发育早期就具备更高自尊心的孩子。

sentences.en: They also have higher emotional understanding,
sentences.zh: 他们也拥有更高的情绪理解力，

sentences.en: because so many of the events that we talk about are emotional.
sentences.zh: 因为我们谈论的许多事件都带有情感色彩。

sentences.en: So I was talking with my colleague, Marshall Duke,
sentences.zh: 当时我正与我的同事马歇尔·杜克交谈，

sentences.en: talking about the power of these early conversations
sentences.zh: 讨论这些早期对话的力量，

sentences.en: and how important it was for children to build up their own narrative story,
sentences.zh: 以及孩子们建立自己的叙事故事有多么重要，

sentences.en: the story of who they are.
sentences.zh: 也就是关于他们是谁的故事。

sentences.en: Marshall's a clinical psychologist, and he said,
sentences.zh: 马歇尔是一位临床心理学家，他说，

sentences.en: but I bet that what's equally important is how families talk about the family past,
sentences.zh: 但我敢说，同样重要的是家庭如何谈论家庭往事，

sentences.en: Coming from the family I did, I was like,
sentences.zh: 出身于我这样的家庭，我当时想，

sentences.en: I don't think that matters as much.
I really think that that's not as important.
sentences.zh: 我真的认为那没那么重要。
于是我们进行了这次谈话，

sentences.en: and we were part of a big funded research program.
sentences.zh: 我们当时参与了一个大型资助研究项目。

sentences.en: We had the means to do this.
sentences.zh: 我们有条件去做这件事。

sentences.en: We said, let's use our resources to figure this out.
sentences.zh: 我们说，让我们利用资源来弄清楚这一点。

sentences.en: So that's when we decided to just tape record families
sentences.zh: 所以我们决定录下家庭的谈话，

sentences.en: talking over the dinner table to see what they talk about.
sentences.zh: 看看他们在餐桌上都聊些什么。

sentences.en: So we tape recorded these families,
sentences.zh: 我们录下了这些家庭的谈话，

sentences.en: and we simply asked them, you know,
sentences.zh: 我们只是简单地告诉他们，你知道的，
